name: What is an Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) and why would I consider one for my property?

mainEntity.name: What is an Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) and why would I consider one for my property?

acceptedAnswer.text: An Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) is a secondary housing unit on a single-family residential lot. It can be attached to the primary home or be a detached structure in your backyard. Homeowners often consider an ADU to add living space for family members, generate rental income, or create a dedicated home office or studio. AKN Design Group specializes in integrating these substantial additions seamlessly with your existing property, ensuring the new structure enhances both functionality and aesthetic value.
acceptedAnswer.description: An ADU is a secondary housing unit on a residential lot, often used for family, rental income, or dedicated workspaces.
